page.title: Help · status bar
page.intro: What each part of the Claude Code status bar means.

sections.title: Line 1 · model and git
rows: Active model and, in parentheses, the reasoning effort level.
You are inside a specific agent.
Local commits you have not pushed yet.
Remote commits you have not pulled yet.
Modified files that are not staged.
The branch's pull request. Green = approved, red = changes requested, yellow = pending.
Vim mode of the Claude Code prompt, when vim mode is enabled.

sections.title: Line 2 · usage
rows: How full the conversation context is, with tokens used/total. Green < 50%, yellow < 80%, red from 80%. When it gets red, run /compact or /clear.
Usage of your subscription's 5-hour limit and countdown until it resets (↻now = already reset). Same colors as ctx.
Usage of the weekly limit and countdown until it resets. Same colors as ctx.
Session cost. Green < $1, yellow < $5, red from $5.
Subscription mode (Claude Code reports your usage limits): the cost is only the API-equivalent value, not money you pay, so it is dimmed, has no colors and there is no $/h rate.
Spend rate per hour, shown after 5 min of session. Grey below STATUSLINE_BURN_WARN (default $15/h), yellow from there, red from STATUSLINE_BURN_HIGH (default $30/h).
Share of the prompt that was served from the prompt cache, which is cheaper. Green ≥ 70%, yellow ≥ 40%, red below.

Time at which the prompt cache expires, as reported by Claude Code (exact, also for the 1-hour cache). Older versions of Claude Code do not report it, and then it is estimated as 5 min after the last activity. Green while more than 1 min is left, then yellow.
In red: the prompt cache expired at that time. The next prompt has to rebuild it, which costs more (see the warning line).
Lines of code added (green) and deleted (red) in the session.

sections.title: Warning line · only when needed
rows: Appears between lines 2 and 3 when the cache has expired and the context is large (≥ 50k tokens). The next prompt will re-cache all of it; it shows the estimated cost. Running /compact first makes that cheaper.

sections.title: Line 3 · changed files
rows: List of every file changed against HEAD. Cmd+click one to see its diff in the browser.
Appears when there are more changed files than STATUSLINE_MAX_FILES. Cmd+click it to open the page with all of them.
Count mode: the total and how many files per status. Cmd+click it to open the page with all of them.

sections.title: Good to know
rows: Anything Claude Code does not report (for example the 5h/7d limits without a subscription) is simply not shown.
Links carry a secret token. Do not share them or paste them in screenshots. If one stops working (403), click a fresh link from the bar.
How the file list is shown: full (all files), compact (default: the first STATUSLINE_MAX_FILES, 10 by default, plus a +N more link), count (only the totals) or off.
Spend rate in USD per hour from which $N/h turns yellow / red (defaults 15 and 30, arbitrary: set what is a lot for you).

Price per million tokens used to estimate the re-cache cost. By default the 5-minute cache-write price of the active model from Anthropic's pricing page (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing).

auto (default), api or subscription. auto picks subscription when Claude Code reports usage limits (Pro/Max plans) and api otherwise; set it to force one. In subscription mode a cold cache is reported as usage limit instead of money.
Language of the bar and of this page: en, es, fr, pt or de. It is chosen when you run install.sh; change it with ./install.sh --lang fr, or override it with this variable.
Run ./statusline.sh --doctor in the install folder; it checks the dependencies and prints the version and state folder.
